clue.text: Feature of boils? Varied help given by good doctor, note

indicators.note: something varied has been changed about, so the following word's letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
G is the standard abbreviation for good
MO is a medical officer
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a patient's boils with a range of remedies and a written note.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: a boil is one example of the condition rather than the condition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmon is a spreading inflammation of tissue, the kind of swelling found in boils and abscesses.

clue.text: Scots tip badly, retaining control — it's a game involving coins

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and jumbled, so the two preceding words have their letters scrambled
retaining means keeping hold of, so the jumbled letters wrap around another piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
to have a hand in something is to have control of it

explanation.surface: A Scotsman leaves a poor tip but keeps his composure, while a coin-flipping game goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch and toss is a gambling game: coins are pitched at a mark, and the nearest player tosses them all, keeping those landing heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch and toss is played by throwing coins at a target and then flipping them, so coins are central to the game.

clue.text: Aussie cheers stop, pair getting run out in the middle

indicators.note: something in the middle sits inside, so this piece goes within the pair

blocks.note: ho is a call to stop
in cricket a pair is two ducks, two zeros
ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: An Australian cricket crowd's celebrations end when a batting pair suffer a run-out mid-pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is not applause but goodbye; HOOROO is Australian slang for farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooroo is an Australian informal farewell, and cheers is likewise used colloquially to say goodbye.

clue.text: Disabled person, one restricted by withered arm and leg

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; 'and' only joins them

explanation.surface: Someone with a withered arm and leg has limited mobility.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMIGER (also lameter) is an old Scots and northern dialect word for a cripple.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamiger is a lame or crippled person, so it names a disabled person in old dialect.

clue.text: See runs round circuit in passing

a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: Watch the runner lap the track as he goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: Chambers allows ELAPSE as the passing of time, so 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, elapse means the passage or lapse of time, which is a passing.

clue.text: Delay, often unjustifiable, involving fool in apparatus?

indicators.note: involving means taking in or including, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: mora is the legal term for culpable delay
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool in a laboratory causes a pointless hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Massora (Masorah) is the body of textual notes on the Hebrew Bible: a critical apparatus, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars call a set of textual notes and variant readings a critical apparatus, which is what the Massora provides.

clue.text: Stranger turning up, some stared, doubtful

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the answer is a run of letters within the next words

explanation.surface: A stranger arrives, and some people stare at him with suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for a newcomer, but it is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger as an adjective means more unusual, the same as odder.

clue.text: Varieties Bedser bowled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

clue.text: People with onset of gout giving work up, old

the first letter of the word

clue.text: Ingredient of salad chopped in, vinegared? This grain possibly

explanation.walkthrough: This is a compound anagram: the answer plus GRAIN together rearrange the letters of 'in, vinegared'.

clue.text: Type of country wherein cowboys appear to take flight (12, two words)

to wing is to fly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a land, but it is country music; Western swing is a dance-band style of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Western swing is a subgenre of country music, blending it with jazz-style swing.

clue.text: E.g. Sturgeon organizing real end with English (twice!)

indicators.note: organizing means putting things into a fresh order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon, a woman who led the Scottish government, is an example of a female political leader.

clue.text: Host? One may be ordered —— the barricades

definitions.text: One may be ordered —— the barricades

blocks.note: first meaning: a Mongol or Tatar military division of ten thousand men

blocks.clueFragment: One may be ordered —— the barricades
blocks.note: second meaning: read as two words, the phrase that fills the gap before 'the barricades'

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a fill-in-the-blank: a soldier may be ordered 'to man the barricades', and the missing words run together into one.
explanation.definitionFit: A toman was a unit of ten thousand soldiers in Mongol armies, and a host is an army or great multitude.

clue.text: Stoops for slugs of Scotch

blocks.note: first meaning: leans or bows the body over
second meaning: in Scots dialect, pulls or swigs of drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, but it signals a Scots word: in Scotland a bend is a hearty drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means bows down or stoops, and the Scots noun means a good pull of liquor.

clue.text: Gordon Bennett howls, penning what's central in paper

asks only for the letter at the exact middle of the following word

the middle letter of a five-letter word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon Bennett' looks like a person, but it is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'good grief'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British exclamations of astonishment, so either can replace the other.

clue.text: Former writ union reversed on being brought in

explanation.walkthrough: An elegit was an old English writ of execution letting a creditor take a debtor's land.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegit is the name of an obsolete writ, so it is a former writ by definition.

clue.text: Line for curlers uses all of central part

blocks.note: to hog something is to take all of it
the core is the centre

explanation.surface: A curling team exhausts the central part of the rink.
explanation.walkthrough: In curling, a stone must cross the hog line (or hog score) to stay in play.
explanation.definitionFit: The hog score is a marked line on a curling rink that a delivered stone must pass.

clue.text: No hawk took the plunge over the pond

definitions.text: took the plunge over the pond

blocks.note: first meaning: a peace-lover, the opposite of a political hawk

blocks.clueFragment: took the plunge over the pond
blocks.note: second meaning: the American past tense of dive

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the pond' means in America, across the Atlantic, where 'dove' is used instead of 'dived'.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a dove favours peace, unlike a hawk; and Americans say a diver dove into the water.

clue.text: Doctor, greats disposed of — one accelerates fast

blocks.note: Dr is the standard abbreviation for doctor
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed of' reads as got rid of, which tempts a deletion, but nothing is removed: it means arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragster is a car built for drag racing, short sprints won by sheer acceleration.

clue.text: Attractive ring's left by way of deposits

indicators.note: left means departed, so that piece goes away from the longer word

the piece to be removed

clue.text: Composer making money in form of art associated with Italy

clue.text: Sea creatures Scottish relative trapped snarl wildly

Scots form of the relative pronoun who

clue.text: Spinners pitching one in part of surface

explanation.definitionFit: Aranea denotes spiders, creatures that spin webs, so they are spinners.

clue.text: Notorious 'sexter', one detained, to begin again from the bottom!

explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Weiner, a former US congressman, was disgraced and later jailed over sexting scandals.

clue.text: Rising mire, hindrance for little duck

explanation.definitionFit: Goslets are tiny waterfowl, the pygmy geese, which are really small perching ducks.

clue.text: Rocky? That star name (all forgotten)?

clue.text: Caledonian bear deserted local enclosure?

clue.text: Components of a world miscellany?
